scope: Unmodified real coordinator and RunSchedule assertions through the official headed Linux runner; virtual transport time, no multi-box claim.
property: An otherwise healthy playing survivor waits at most 50 ms while preserving the directory-decided equal-half authority.
causes: A two-seat partition leaves one live seat: neither equal half has an independent majority.
The design gives the assigned directory the first decision for that split; a pending answer is not authority.
A hung host cannot itself ask or deliver a new decision.
A fresh 100 ms directory round trip exceeds the 2-tick link buffer plus 50 ms in the exact schedule.
With a 30 ms peer link and a 300 ms directory exchange, even the permitted maximum six ticks (100 ms) plus the 50 ms wait bound totals only 150 ms.

unresolved: The complete gate needs a revised authority/availability contract or a different authorized fault bound. Increasing delay, guessing authority, discarding a survivor, or loosening the fixture would violate the current requirements.
limits: This explains the pending-directory bound conflict only. It does not excuse four-seat startup holds, return pacing, B3 noise failures or every other red row.
The 300 ms original exchange also retries after its 250 ms request timeout; removing that retry would still leave an ideal 252 ms wait in this recorded schedule.

The earlier silent-link schedule is retained GREEN separately because the isolated but running host wins authority and the other seat is held; it is not evidence of a healthy survivor satisfying the bound.
